Subject: Quick: mid-contract uplift + co-term alignment

Hi Stephanie —

We had an internal spike in usage over the last month and are looking at a mid-contract expansion ahead of our renewal. Two asks: 1) can Redwood do a short-term uplift with a taper (so we don't overcommit if usage drops), and 2) we'd prefer to align the new capacity to our renewal date so everything co-terms.

We have procurement windows and would need something that won't require a full contract amendment (procurement prefers limited SOWs or amendment riders). Happy to jump on a call — cc'ing Matt who owns procurement.

Thanks,
Anne

Head of Platform, BrightCore.ai

Subject: Re: Quick: mid-contract uplift + co-term alignment

Hi Anne —

Thanks for the heads-up — glad to see the spike. We can absolutely support a short-term uplift with a decreasing corridor (we call it a flexible corridor + escape-hatch). High level options:

- Option A: 90-day uplift bucket (reserved units) that steps down by 25% each 30 days if observed usage decays. No amendment needed; we issue an addendum rider and one-off invoice.
- Option B: 6-month uplift with monthly reconciliation and a 60% usage floor to keep price protection. This requires a simple amendment for co-terming at renewal.
- Option C: On-demand burst credits with priority queueing (higher per-token rate) — lowest friction but higher unit cost.

I've looped in Ben to pull a capacity/pricing sketch and Laura for billing implications. Can you share the target uplift (TPU equivalent or token budget) so we can sketch numbers? If you prefer a call, we're free tomorrow between 10–1 PT.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Folks —

Draft numbers attached. Two important constraints from finance: 1) we need a minimum uplift commit to qualify for the stepped discount (we suggested 20% over baseline for Option A), and 2) if co-terming requires crediting unused reserved units, the simplest path is to convert unused uplift into a prepaid credit usable until renewal then reconciled.

Highlights in the workbook: 
- Tab 1: 90-day corridor math (25% step-down)
- Tab 2: 6-month annualize when co-term (pro-rated conversion)
- Tab 3: burst credit SKU pricing (per-token uplift)

I've flagged the legal checklist — this is a 1-page addendum and procurement should be okay. Laura, can you confirm invoice treatment (one-off vs amortized) and tax handling?

-Ben
